content: I had really tight pulley, had to push it inside the shaft with water pump pliers.

Just going to leave this in here incase it's useful for support. I upgraded a MK4S to a Core One, and had the same issues getting these on during that upgrade, and just as much if not more doing it for the INDX/Gen2 upgrade. I think there might be a batch of motors out there where the shaft has a slightly larger thickness that makes pulley's almost impossible to put on without excessive force. I loosened the grub screws, and even attempt to sand out any burrs that might have been in there. I still had to break out a hammer and use a hex bit adapter to tap this particular one down enough to touch the spacing tool. Considering that these pulleys are probably the easiest thing to adjust, I'd suggest making them only fractionally larger so they actually slip on easily, and let the grub screws do the rest. As it stands I questioned if I even needed to bother with the grub screws once I forced the thing on. I tightened them anyway though. I fear I won't be able to remove this one if I ever have to upgrade the pulley or the motor for any future upgrades.
I just installed the pulleys on both motors, had no issues. They just slid onto the shaft.
Both pulleys indeed very tight, it was hard to put it on the shaft. I removed both grub screws completely before trying to slide it on.
I needed to use a c-clamp to get the pulley on.  It's way too tight.
IMPORTANT - this pulley is oriented opposite of right pulley.  Make sure to match pictures.  Not that I would have made this error

replies.content: jebas, thanks, would have realised this very late..

content: Why is everyone hammering on their pulleys? Was it impossible to loosen the set screw to slide on and then retighten? Am I missing something? I just slightly loosened and then retightened...?

replies.content: +1 on being able to remove the set screw without any issues. I wonder if there were a few batches that had the torque set too high for these.
+1 for me as well. I had no issues removing the original pulleys (which I installed when I built the original Core One kit), and installing the new ones. Pulley tolerances were fine.

Set screws came out just fine.  My issue was the set screw caused a small sliver of metal to protrude from the drive shaft.  Which made it difficult to remove the pulley.

I filed the high spots with a fine file afterwards and the new ones went on easily.

content: I will never remove this pulley anymore. It doesnt need to be this tight... everything started with the C1, MK4 they would slide easily... what's going on?

Like others said the tolerance on the pulleys is insanely small.  You have to use a crazy amount of force to get these on.  They are basically scratching a. groove into the shaft at this point.  There is zero chance I will ever be able to remove these again after putting them on without breaking the motor that is how tight they are.  There is something wrong with the pulleys for sure. Took me 1 hour to get both on.
I had to use a 5.0Z rival on the pulley, and then it fit. But it was not a problem on the right side ???
The provided pulley was way too tight, really bad tolerance and quality. Needed a hammer, hopefully I did not damaged my motor...

Yeah so my pulley was so tight it was impossible to install. then it was absurdly hard to remove and i had to pry with a hammer. 
Had to drill then pulley with a 5mm drill to make it fit... The diameter was only 4,9mm when it should have been 5.
Note that the part of the pulley with the grub screws is AWAY from the motor. It's important to get this orientation correct.

replies.content: Good catch! We’ve added this important detail to the instructions.
